decisions.reason: A classic lever handle that fits the firm's core range was launched only a year ago and has visible website presence, so management will keep it and attribute any slow start to normal market ramp-up.
A lever handle family takes significant tooling and design investment and supports the firm's system-breadth strategy, which favors continued commitment.
This door handle design sits close to the established offer, carries sunk design costs and is publicly listed, so dropping it after one year would be premature.
Design investment and public listing argue for persistence, and early results can still be explained by temporary launch effects.
As a handle family that broadens the system portfolio with substantial invested resources, management will stay committed.
The L700 electronic access system was promoted publicly as unique and is central to the announced digital building direction, so escalation of commitment strongly favors keeping it.
